🔥🇲🇽 <u>NOW MEXICO WANTS GARCÍA LUNA'S WIFE TOO</u>

President Sheinbaum confirmed Mexico has asked Washington to detain and extradite Linda Cristina Pereyra, wife of jailed ex-security czar Genaro García Luna, on money-laundering and organized-crime charges. The FGR says she was part of a 50-person network that rigged federal prison contracts, costing the treasury over 5.1 billion pesos. This time it's Mexico handing the US the extradition order.

🇲🇽🗳️ <u>MORENA SLAMS THE DOOR ON PARTY-JUMPERS</u>

Ahead of the 2027 elections, Morena created a commission to vet every politician defecting from other parties before they can register. "These types of characters must be evaluated by us," said national leader Ariadna Montiel, after state leaders flagged ex-PRI and ex-PAN mayors trying to climb aboard — a party that has grown from 2.3 to 11.6 million members and polls at 52% for next year's deputy races.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>"BRIBE MY STAFF AND I'LL SHUT YOU DOWN"</u>

Interior Secretary Rosa Icela Rodríguez put casino operators on notice: "Don't corrupt Segob personnel, because I'll close your businesses and I'll jail the colleagues taking your money." Around 13 casinos have already been shut, with several under investigation by the FGR and Financial Intelligence Unit for money laundering — as she moves to replace a gaming law that dates back to 1947.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>MEXICAN NAVY DISMANTLES ONE OF ITS BIGGEST METH LABS EVER</u>

The Navy seized more than 16 tons of methamphetamine and took down a 5,700 m² clandestine megalab in Sinaloa — the second-largest found under this government — a $347 million hit to organized crime in a single operation. Security chief Omar García Harfuch said the strike, led by Mexico's own Naval Intelligence, also recovered over 10 tons of chemical precursors.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>MEXICO HOLDS THE KEY TO CANADA'S RETURN TO T-MEC</u>

With Washington and Ottawa at each other's throats, it's Mexico keeping the T-MEC review on track to close before year's end. Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard is in formal talks to bring Canada back into the negotiating rounds, warning that "tensions between the US and Canada don't help" North America. The partner everyone wrote off is now brokering the deal.

💵🇲🇽 <u>Remittances hit $5.57 billion in July — a sixth straight month of growth despite the US crackdown</u>

Mexicans abroad sent home $5,570.6 million in July, up about 3% year-on-year and the sixth consecutive monthly increase, according to Banxico figures reported by El Financiero. That lifts January–July to $36.3 billion, above the $35.2 billion of the same stretch in 2025 — even as ICE raids and visa purges target the very workers wiring the money. The average transfer held at $426, the paycheck millions of Mexican households still count on.
